from.place: The derived couple construction is functorial in the couple; iterating gives maps on all E_r and at infinity

title: Functoriality of derived exact couples
statement: Let $(D,E,\alpha,f,g)$ and $(D',E',\alpha',f',g')$ be exact couples [def-sp-exact-couple] in the same abelian category. Suppose maps $t_D:D\to D'$ and $t_E:E\to E'$ preserve bidegrees and satisfy $t_D\alpha=\alpha't_D$, $t_Df=f't_E$, and $t_Eg=g't_D$ (that is, they form a morphism of exact couples). Then the maps induced by $(t_D,t_E)$ on the derived couples are well defined and commute with the derived structure maps. Iterating the construction gives a morphism on every page $E_r$ commuting with $d_r$, and the induced map carries $Z_\infty$ into $Z'_\infty$ and $B_\infty$ into $B'_\infty$, hence induces a morphism $E_\infty\to E'_\infty$ as in [def-sp-convergence].
